title: Discharge Summary
key_sentences: Mr Halvorsen presented to the emergency department with a four-day history of productive cough, fever and increasing shortness of breath.
On arrival his oxygen saturation was 89% on room air and his temperature was 38.9 °C.
A chest radiograph showed consolidation in the right lower zone without effusion.
He was treated with intravenous amoxicillin and oral clarithromycin, and was switched to oral antibiotics on day three once his fever had settled.
He was mobilising independently and maintaining saturations above 94% on room air at the time of discharge.
Complete the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
Seek urgent medical help if you become more breathless, develop chest pain or cough up blood.

rows: Dr. Paul Mercer, Eastside Medical Practice

list_items.text: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe (primary diagnosis)
Renal function and potassium check in one week at the family doctor’s practice.
Repeat chest radiograph in six weeks, to be requested by the family doctor.
Diabetes nurse review of glucose control within one month.
